proof.definition: Delta_ij = Fraction.from_float(saved_H[embed_i,embed_j]) - Fraction.from_float(baseline_H[i,j]); subtract exact represented binary64 operands, never a rounded subtraction.
proof.row_sum: For all 1595 rows and every mathematically nonzero entry: r_i=sum_j abs(Delta_ij) exactly in Fraction. rho=max_i r_i; also each complete sector rho_s. Save all exact row ratios, affected rows, entry count/max and symmetry checks.
proof.proof: Both matrices are finite real symmetric. For any eigenvector of Delta, choose its largest component: abs(lambda)<=max row absolute sum=rho, hence norm2(Delta)<=rho. Injecting this old-block Delta into the full2574 space preserves the nonzero spectrum and gives the same norm bound. Variational min-max bounds each ordered eigenvalue change by its sector rho_s.
proof.comparison_operator: Only a conceptual finite K=H_saved-E Delta E^T for the theorem. Never construct, save, diagonalize, inject or use K; all actual old-to-new Q couplings and new Q-Q entries remain the native saved values.
proof.excitation_bound: For fixed ordered upper/lower sector roots, absolute change due solely to nested arithmetic <=rho_upper+rho_lower. Centroid uses declared (2J+1) weights; splitting <=rho_a+rho_b. Bound is for exact finite matrix eigenvalues, excludes numerical eigensolver error, physical truncation error and physical-state re-identification under hypothetical K.
proof.units: Hartree exact dyadic ratios; cm^-1 bound uses the exact rational of the represented native HARTREE_CM1 scalar, not a metrological constant interval.
proof.display: Convert exact nonnegative Fraction to binary64 then nextafter(+infinity) when needed; preserve exact numerator/denominator and upward display hex. No heuristic norm or estimated roundoff bound.
